issues.t: Engine oil sludge (oil gel)
issues.sym: The oil light flickers or comes on, the engine smokes or burns oil, runs rough, or knocks. Dark, thick oil on the dipstick. In bad cases the engine seizes.
issues.why: Oil on these 2.2L and 3.0L V6 engines can thicken into a tar-like gel, especially when oil changes are stretched out. The gel blocks oil passages and starves the engine. Toyota once ran a special coverage program for this on 1997-2002 cars with these engines.
issues.next: If the oil light comes on, stop and check the oil. Have a shop pull the oil filler cap or valve cover to look for sludge. Caught early, a cleaning and frequent oil changes can save the engine; a seized engine needs replacing.

issues.t: Stripped cylinder head bolt threads
issues.sym: Coolant slowly disappears with no visible leak, the engine overheats, or there is white exhaust smoke. It can look like a blown head gasket.
issues.why: The threads for the head bolts in the 2.4L aluminum engine block can stretch or pull out, letting the head gasket lose its clamp. Coolant then leaks out or into the cylinders.
issues.next: Watch the coolant level and temperature gauge. If coolant keeps dropping, have a cooling system pressure test and a block test done. The fix is to install thread inserts in the block and a new head gasket.

issues.t: Excessive oil consumption
issues.sym: You need to add a quart of oil every 1,000-2,000 miles, the low oil light comes on between changes, or the engine runs low before the next service.
issues.why: On the 2.4L engine the piston oil rings can clog with carbon and let oil burn in the cylinders. Toyota ran warranty enhancement ZE7 for 2007-2008 Solaras with this engine and replaced pistons and rings; that program has ended.
issues.next: Check the oil every fill-up and keep it topped up so the engine never runs low. Ask a shop to do an oil consumption test. Ask a Toyota dealer if any goodwill help is offered.

issues.t: Sticky, melting or cracked dashboard
issues.sym: The top of the dashboard turns shiny and sticky, cracks, or gets gummy. It can throw a bright glare onto the windshield that makes it hard to see in sunlight.
issues.why: The dashboard material breaks down with heat and sunlight. Toyota covered 2004-2008 Solara dashboards under warranty enhancement ZE6, which ran for 10 years from the original sale date and has now ended for nearly all cars.
issues.next: Use a sunshade and a matte dash cover to cut the glare. A cracked dash over the passenger airbag should be replaced. Ask a Toyota dealer with your VIN about any remaining goodwill coverage.

issues.t: Convertible top tears, shrinks or lets in water
issues.sym: The fabric top splits at a seam, the rear glass sags or comes loose, the headliner drops, or water drips inside when it rains.
issues.why: Age and sun dry out the top fabric, glue and the seal around the rear window. Once the seams or glass seal let go, water gets in.
issues.next: Keep the top clean and dry and park out of the sun when you can. Small tears can be patched, but a loose rear window or shredded fabric usually means a new top. Dry out wet carpet quickly to avoid mold.

issues.t: Convertible top pops or its boot comes apart
issues.sym: A popping noise when the convertible top opens, or the cover (boot) that hides the folded top separates at its seams.
issues.why: Toyota issued bulletins for these early Solara convertibles for a popping top mechanism and for the boot separating at its reinforcement, with a repair kit.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer or convertible top shop check it against the bulletins. The boot can usually be repaired with the kit rather than replaced.

issues.t: Rear speaker hums or rattles on convertibles
issues.sym: A humming or rattling sound from the rear woofer speaker area, mostly on convertibles.
issues.why: Toyota put out bulletins for the rear woofer humming or rattling on some of these cars.
issues.next: Have a dealer or audio shop check the rear woofer and its mounting. It is not a safety issue.

issues.t: Wind noise from the convertible top
issues.sym: Loud whistling or rushing wind noise around the convertible top at highway speed.
issues.why: Toyota released a bulletin in 2004 to reduce wind noise from the new-generation convertible top, usually by adjusting the top and its seals.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer or convertible top shop to check the top fit and seals against the bulletin.

issues.t: Crankshaft pulley outer ring can slip (recall)
issues.sym: A squeal or noise from the engine belt area, a battery warning light, or suddenly heavy steering if the belt comes off.
issues.why: Not enough adhesive was used in the crankshaft pulley on some V6 engines built mid-2004 to early 2005. The outer ring can shift and throw the power steering belt. Recall 11V-539.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check your VIN. If the belt comes off you lose power steering and charging, so pull over safely. The dealer replaces the pulley for free.

issues.t: Rear axle may be weak from improper heat treatment (recall)
issues.sym: Usually no early warning. In time a rear axle part could crack or break, causing noise, wobble or loss of control.
issues.why: Some rear axle hub parts were not heat-treated properly and may be too weak. Recall 00V-154 covered a small number of cars.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer run your VIN. The dealer inspects and replaces the rear axle hub assemblies free.

issues.t: Side curtain airbag strap may be misrouted (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign. In a side crash or rollover the front of the curtain airbag may not open fully.
issues.why: On a small number of 2007 Solaras the tether strap for the curtain airbag was routed wrong. Recall 06V-488.
issues.next: Have a Toyota dealer check your VIN. The dealer inspects both straps and reroutes them for free.

issues.t: Add-on seat heaters can short and burn the seat (recall)
issues.sym: A burning smell from the seat, a seat heater that stops working, or scorch marks on the seat fabric.
issues.why: Dealer-installed accessory seat heaters with copper strand elements can have their wiring damaged when the seat cushion is pressed down, causing a short and a fire risk. Recall 16V-396.
issues.next: Stop using the seat heater. Have a Toyota dealer check your VIN; they disconnect the heater.

issues.t: Tire load label may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: There is no load-carrying capacity label on the door jamb, so you may not know the safe weight limit.
issues.why: Some cars sold through Gulf States Toyota left without the required load label. Recall 10V-035.
issues.next: Check the driver door jamb for the label. If it is missing, a Toyota dealer will supply one free.

issues.t: Check engine light from a failed oxygen or air-fuel sensor
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, often with a small drop in fuel mileage. The car may still run normally.
issues.why: The front oxygen or air-fuel ratio sensor (or its built-in heater) wears out. Toyota issued bulletins for sensor heater codes and lean codes such as P0171, P0174 and P2195 on these cars. Owners most often report it past 100,000 miles.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A sensor or heater code usually means replacing that sensor. Lean codes should also be checked for vacuum leaks or a dirty air flow sensor before parts are swapped.

issues.t: Check engine light for an EVAP vapor leak
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with a code like P0456 (small evaporative leak), sometimes after refueling. The car drives normally.
issues.why: The fuel vapor system is not holding pressure. A loose or worn gas cap is the most common cause; cracked hoses or a vent valve can also do it. Toyota issued bulletins on this code and on fuel getting into the EVAP system.
issues.next: Tighten the gas cap until it clicks, or replace it if the seal is cracked. If the light comes back, have a smoke test done to find the leak.

issues.t: Rotten egg (sulfur) smell from the exhaust
issues.sym: A rotten egg smell from the tailpipe, mostly after hard acceleration or when the engine is warmed up.
issues.why: The catalytic converter can give off a sulfur smell depending on the fuel. Toyota issued bulletins for sulfur odor on these cars; a rich-running engine makes it worse.
issues.next: Try a different brand of gas for a few tanks. If the smell stays or the check engine light comes on, have the engine checked for running rich and the converter tested.

issues.t: Harsh or jerky automatic shifts
issues.sym: The automatic slams into gear, shifts late, or feels jerky, especially at low speed or when cold.
issues.why: The transmission control software on these cars can cause rough shifts. Toyota released an engine computer update to improve shift smoothness. Low or old fluid also makes shifting worse.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and condition. Ask a Toyota dealer whether a software update applies to your car. Keep up with fluid changes.

issues.t: Check engine light for random misfire (P0300)
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, sometimes flashing, and the engine shakes or idles rough.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin for random misfire codes on these years. Worn spark plugs or ignition parts, vacuum leaks, or dirty fuel injectors can cause it.
issues.next: If the light is flashing, drive gently and get it checked soon. A shop should read the codes, check the plugs and ignition, and follow the bulletin.

issues.t: Airbag (SRS) warning light stays on
issues.sym: The airbag warning light on the dash comes on and stays on, sometimes on and off.
issues.why: Loose or corroded connectors under the front seats for the side airbags and seat belt parts are a common cause. Toyota issued a manual update for side airbag circuit codes B1821 and B1826.
issues.next: Airbags may not work right while this light is on. Have the SRS codes read and the seat connectors checked; avoid moving the seats roughly over the wiring.

issues.t: Moonroof rubbing or shuddering noise
issues.sym: A rubbing, grinding or shuddering noise when the moonroof opens or closes.
issues.why: Toyota issued a bulletin in 2004 for this noise on the moonroof of the new-generation Solara.
issues.next: Ask a Toyota dealer or body shop to service the moonroof per the bulletin. Clean and lube the tracks.

issues.t: Rear suspension noise
issues.sym: A clunk, squeak or rattle from the rear of the car over bumps.
issues.why: Toyota released a bulletin in 2004 for noise from the rear suspension of these cars.
issues.next: Have a shop check the rear suspension and follow the bulletin. Also check sway bar links and strut mounts.

issues.t: Tire pressure warning light after tire work
issues.sym: The tire pressure warning light comes on or stays on after rotating, replacing or inflating tires.
issues.why: The tire pressure system has to be re-initialized when tires or pressures change. Toyota put out bulletins on how to reset it. A failing sensor battery can also set the light.
issues.next: Set all tires to the pressure on the door label, then reset the system (or have a shop do it). If the light stays on, have each sensor tested.

issues.t: Valve cover gasket oil leak
issues.sym: Oil seeping on the top or sides of the engine, a burning oil smell after driving, or oil around the spark plug tubes.
issues.why: The rubber valve cover gaskets and spark plug tube seals harden with age and heat on these Camry-based engines and start to seep.
issues.next: Have the gasket replaced before oil drips onto the hot exhaust. On the V6 the job takes longer because of the intake.

issues.t: Water pump leaks coolant
issues.sym: Pink or green coolant drips under the front of the engine, a sweet smell, or the coolant level slowly drops.
issues.why: The water pump seal wears out on these Camry-platform engines. On the V6 the pump is driven by the timing belt, so it is usually changed with the belt.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the coolant and temperature gauge. Replace the pump before it fails; on the V6 or 2.2L, do it together with the timing belt to save labor.

issues.t: Knocking from worn front strut mounts and sway bar links
issues.sym: A knock or clunk from the front over bumps, or a creak when turning.
issues.why: The front strut mounts and stabilizer (sway bar) links wear out with age and mileage on these Camry-based cars.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked. Links are a simple fix; worn mounts are often replaced along with the struts.

issues.t: Timing belt wears out or snaps
issues.sym: Often no warning: the engine suddenly quits while driving and cranks but won't start. Sometimes a ticking or slapping sound comes first.
issues.why: The 2.2L and both V6 engines use a rubber timing belt that must be replaced on schedule (about every 90,000 miles or so). An old or oil-soaked belt can break.
issues.next: Check your records. If there is no proof the belt was changed, have it done along with the water pump and tensioner. If it already broke, have the engine checked before replacing the belt.

issues.t: Water leaks from the sunroof or in heavy rain
issues.sym: Wet carpet, water dripping from the headliner, or a musty smell after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: The sunroof drain tubes clog with dirt and leaves, and door and window seals age, so water overflows into the cabin.
issues.next: Clear the sunroof drains with compressed air or a trimmer line. Check and replace worn seals. Dry out wet carpet quickly to prevent mold.

issues.t: Paint fading and peeling on the roof and hood
issues.sym: The paint on the roof, hood or trunk goes dull, the clear coat flakes off, or paint chips away.
issues.why: Sun exposure breaks down the clear coat on the horizontal panels over time.
issues.next: Wash and wax regularly and park in shade. Once clear coat peels, the only real fix is repainting the panel.

issues.t: Engine surges or accelerates unevenly
issues.sym: The engine speed rises and falls on its own, or acceleration feels lumpy and uneven.
issues.why: A dirty throttle body, vacuum leak or failing engine sensor can make the idle and throttle response uneven on these cars.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the throttle body cleaned. If the car surges forward on its own, use the brakes firmly, shift to neutral if needed, and get it checked right away.

issues.t: Car pulls or does not track straight
issues.sym: The car drifts to one side on a straight road, or the steering wheel is off-center.
issues.why: Owners report alignment and tracking complaints on this generation. Worn tires, alignment, or a tire with a shifted belt are common causes.
issues.next: Swap the front tires side to side to see if the pull moves. Then have the alignment checked and tires inspected.
